ev_find:
LFU beat LRU in 19 of 20 workload and size pairs measured here; on the real hour by 9.9, 10.1, 8.3, 4.6 points at 20k, 50k, 100k and 200k keys. These traces have steady popularity and no bursts inside an hour, which is where frequency wins.
Hour-to-hour drift barely changed that: over six real hours LFU led LRU by 9.5, 9.6, 7.8, 4.3 points. The drift here is mild (85% of each hour's top 10,000 pages were in the next hour's); a trending-news spike would favour LRU more.
allkeys-lrm behaved like random eviction (within 0.3 points at every size), as it must for cache-aside: a key is written once, at fill time, so "least recently modified" means "filled longest ago", and reads never protect it.
Redis's sampled LRU was within 2.0 points of exact LRU on the real hour (and Redis held about 2% fewer keys than the simulation, its memory limit including per-key overhead), as the docs promise for power-law traffic. Raising maxmemory-samples to 10 moved its hit ratio by at most 0.4 points.
Room left: at 50k keys the offline optimum (OPT) hits 55.1%, against 39.4% for the best Redis policy. And 36.5% of all 2,000,000 requests were the first ever for their key: misses no policy and no memory size can remove.
noeviction kept the keys that arrived first, which under shuffled traffic are mostly popular ones, so its hit ratio looks fine (53.0% at 200k keys) while 781,318 SETs failed with an out-of-memory error. In an application that does not catch that error, every one is a failed request.
volatile-lru with no TTLs is noeviction: 1,328,877 failed SETs and 0 evictions at 50k keys; the same run with a TTL on every key evicted 1,423,822 keys and failed 0 SETs, but held only 39,833 keys in the same memory: a TTL costs memory per key (Redis docs).

Policy		Hit ratio, 50k keys	Work saved (CWHR)	Hit ratio, 200k keys	Work saved (CWHR)
Redis allkeys-lru	measured	29.3%	28.6%	52.0%	51.5%
Redis allkeys-lfu	measured	39.4%	38.7%	56.6%	56.2%
Exact LRU	simulated	31.3%	30.7%	53.0%	52.5%
GreedyDual (knows each miss's cost)	simulated	22.7%	57.4%	49.3%	65.9%
OPT (ignores cost)	simulated	55.1%	54.6%	69.4%	69.0%
Miss costs: 0.189 ms (primary-key lookup) for nine keys in ten, 10.8 ms (usage aggregate) for one in ten, chosen at random. CWHR = (hits on cheap keys × 0.189 + hits on expensive keys × 10.8) / (all requests, same weights).
